configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.description: Configure filtering settings for the SAP LogServ TA.

entity.label: Enable Filtering
entity.help: Controls whether index-time filtering is active. When enabled, incoming log events are evaluated against the Include Filters, Exclude Filters, Include Sources, Exclude Sources, and Days in the Past rules below — events that don't pass are routed to nullQueue and never indexed (no license usage). When disabled, all events are indexed regardless of the filter rules. On a single instance, changes take effect immediately after Save. On a deployment server, changes are staged to deployment-apps/ and a Deploy to Forwarders button appears below.

entity.label: Include Filters
entity.help: Allowlist of log types to index, using comma-separated path patterns. Each pattern matches the log type path (e.g., linux/messages, hana/hanaaudit). Only log types matching at least one pattern will be indexed — everything else is dropped. Default: */* (include all). Examples: hana/* (all HANA logs), linux/messages,proxy/squid (specific types only).

validators.errorMsg: Include filters must be less than 4096 characters.

entity.label: Exclude Filters
entity.help: Blocklist of log types to drop, using comma-separated path patterns. Any log type matching an exclude pattern is dropped — even if it also matches an include pattern (exclude always wins). Leave empty to exclude nothing. Examples: linux/cron,linux/kern (drop cron and kernel logs), dns/* (drop all DNS logs).

validators.errorMsg: Exclude filters must be less than 4096 characters.

entity.label: Include Sources
entity.help: Keep events from these sources even when their folder is not in Include Filters. Comma-separated patterns matched against the event's whole source value, e.g. /usr/sap/*/trace/* or ps. Prefix a folder to limit an entry to it: linux/linux_secure=/var/log/sssd/*. Only used when Include Filters is narrower than */* - with */* everything is already kept. Leave empty for none.

validators.errorMsg: Include Sources must be less than 4096 characters.
Include Sources may contain only letters, numbers, spaces and / . _ : * ? = , + @ ~ - (no quotes, backslashes, brackets or line breaks).

entity.label: Exclude Sources
entity.help: Drop events from these sources, even if their folder is included (excludes always win). Comma-separated patterns matched against the event's whole source value, e.g. /var/log/zypper.log, /var/log/YaST2/*. Prefix a folder to limit an entry to it: linux/linux_secure=/var/log/zypper.log. * matches any run of characters (including /), ? one character; matching is case-sensitive. Leave empty to drop nothing by source.

validators.errorMsg: Exclude Sources must be less than 4096 characters.
Exclude Sources may contain only letters, numbers, spaces and / . _ : * ? = , + @ ~ - (no quotes, backslashes, brackets or line breaks).

entity.label: Days in the Past
entity.help: Only index events from the last N days. The cutoff updates every 24 hours and on each Save, creating a rolling window that moves forward daily. Example with Days in the Past = 7: On March 11, events timestamped March 4 or earlier are dropped. The next day (March 12), the window shifts — now events from March 5 or earlier are dropped. An event from March 5 that was indexed on March 11 would be dropped if re-ingested on March 12. Set to 0 to disable (index all events regardless of age). Useful for preventing bulk backfill of historical data during initial setup or recovery.

validators.errorMsg: Days in the Past must be between 0 and 3650.

entity.label: Cloud Provider
entity.help: Stamp every indexed SAP LogServ event with an indexed cloud_provider field identifying which cloud the data was ingested from. This is an index-time attribution applied on the parsing tier (Heavy Forwarders / Indexer) to ALL events the Data TA routes. Select the provider that matches where THIS tier's SAP ECS data lives. 'Not set' (default) applies no stamp — events carry no cloud_provider field unless your ingest add-on sets one (e.g., the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services sets cloud_provider::azure on its inputs). NOTE: this is a deployment-wide setting; on a single Heavy Forwarder that ingests BOTH AWS and Azure data simultaneously, use per-input attribution instead. On a deployment server, changes are staged to deployment-apps/ and a Deploy to Forwarders button appears below.
